Gora Kalwaria Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Góra Kalwaria, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Góra Kalwaria began after 1802, and by the mid-19th century the town had become headquarters of the Ger Hasidic dynasty, one of the most influential in Poland. By 1921, 2,691 Jews made up nearly half the town's population, deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in February 1941 and murdered at Treblinka the following year. The cemetery, first documented in the town's 1827-1832 budget, holds particular significance for Ger Hasidim: Rabbi Yitzhak Meir Rothenberg Alter, the dynasty's founder and author of 'Chidusze ha-Rim,' was buried here in 1866, joined in 1905 by the third Gerrer Rebbe, Yehuda Arie Lejb, author of 'Sfas Emes.' During WWII, Germans used the cemetery as an execution site for both Jews and Poles, and looted tombstones to pave a Soviet POW camp square. After 1945, the Jewish Committee built a concrete structure over the great rabbis' graves and relocated about 150 tombstones back to the site; the Nissenbaum Family Foundation added a new driveway and fence in 1989, and a new ohel was built by the century's end.
